ggutils

Utility functions for ggplot2. The package starts with a smart axis label guide and is meant to grow: new helpers belong here rather than in a collection of single-purpose packages.

ggutils collects small, reusable helpers that smooth over the rough edges of building plots with ggplot2. They plug into the usual grammar — no new geometry, no special data format — and each one solves a concrete problem.

guide_axis_smart(): readable labels on crowded axes

When a discrete axis carries many categories (50 samples, 200 genes, …) the stock ggplot2 axis draws every label on a single line. The labels overlap, or you rotate them all by 90°, or you hide them and lose the information. guide_axis_smart() is a GuideAxis subclass that takes over label drawing:

  • Choose the labels: which = (integer index / label text / logical vector / function) or n = (auto-pick at most n labels, evenly spaced).
  • Use the page: labels are packed without overlap (smartAlign-style one-dimensional compaction) and distributed over nrow rows (x axis) or columns (y axis). Rows are only added when they are needed: labels stretch along the axis when a single row fits, clustered labels are stacked automatically.
  • Never overlaps: if there is no room left, labels are dropped instead of being printed on top of each other.
  • Leader lines: every displayed label is tied back to its tick, by default with the circlize / ComplexHeatmap::anno_mark() “diagonal” geometry (short perpendicular stub, diagonal, short stub).

coord_spiral(): Cartesian plots on a spiral

coord_spiral() bends an ordinary ggplot into an Archimedean spiral, using the same geometry as spiralize (r = b·theta with one turn per radius unit). The x aesthetic runs along the spiral as the angle, y becomes the radius across the track; lines, bars, points and areas all work. The matching angle and radial axes are drawn automatically, and facet_wrap() / facet_grid() get one spiral per panel.

ggplot(d, aes(x, y)) + geom_line() + coord_spiral()
ggplot(d, aes(x, y)) + geom_line() + facet_wrap(~set) + coord_spiral()

# turns / start angle / track thickness / gap between turns
coord_spiral(turns = 5, start = 0, height = .7)
coord_spiral(turns = 3, gap = .3, clockwise = TRUE)

# fine-tune the two axes: breaks, label rotation, tick length, side
ggplot(d, aes(x, y)) + geom_col() +
  scale_x_spiral_axis(minor_breaks = seq(0, 1, .1)) +
  scale_y_spiral_axis(side = "both", label_rot = 90) +
  coord_spiral(turns = 3)

Every layer that hands its x/y to the coordinate transform works unchanged - lines, areas, bars, histograms, box plots, violins, tiles, text, error bars, segments with arrows. Layers that only carry xend/xmin coordinates (geom_segment(), geom_rect()) are warped too, though the edge between two warped points stays straight. geom_hline() and friends, which have no end points, are not supported.

More ggplot2 utilities will be added here over time. The deliberately broad name means you can load one package instead of keeping track of several single-function ones.

Installation

Requires R >= 4.1 and ggplot2 >= 4.0.0 (the guide API used here was rewritten in ggplot2 4.0).

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("junjunlab/ggutils")

Or, from a local clone of the repository:

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_local(".")
# or, from a shell:
# R CMD INSTALL .

Documentation

The complete reference manual — every function, argument and example — is published on the package documentation site:

  • Reference manual: https://junjunlab.github.io/ggutils/reference/
  • 中文 vignette（入门与全部用法）: https://junjunlab.github.io/ggutils/articles/ggutils.html
  • English vignette: https://junjunlab.github.io/ggutils/articles/ggutils-en.html

The vignettes walk through label selection (which), automatic selection (n), staggered rows (nrow), the three leader-line styles, vertical axes, facets and heatmap annotation; the reference manual documents every argument and default. The layout algorithms smart_align(), box_arrange() and smart_stack() are exported and can also be used on their own.

Credits

The one-dimensional, overlap-free compaction is a port of the smartAlign algorithm from the circlize package; the box arrangement is a port of the ComplexHeatmap package. ggutils only re-uses the algorithms — the ggplot2 guide integration is new.
